query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In untreated Q235 steel, local microstructural heterogeneity—especially the uneven distribution of grain boundaries and inclusions—leads to the formation of inhomogeneous, weakly adherent iron oxide films. This nonuniform passivation promotes localized corrosion onset in harsh, chloride‐rich environments at both room and moderately elevated temperatures. By homogenizing the microstructure (e.g., via thermal annealing), the subsequent oxide layer would form more uniformly by reducing the local electrochemical potential gradients.
generation.material_initial_state: Pre-exposure (as-received) Q235 mild carbon steel with its inherent rolled/forged microstructure exhibiting varying grain sizes, high grain-boundary density areas, and inclusions.
generation.intervention: A controlled thermal annealing treatment designed to reduce microstructural heterogeneity and homogenize the grain size distribution.
generation.conditions: Exposure to a corrosive medium (for example, a chloride solution) at ambient room temperature and at moderately elevated temperatures under controlled laboratory conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The density and distribution of grain boundaries and inclusions that govern the quality and uniformity of the spontaneously formed iron oxide passivation film.
generation.mechanism: Localized microstructural inhomogeneities lead to uneven oxide scale formation, which creates sites with differential electrochemical potentials. These sites become preferential initiation points for pitting and other localized corrosion processes. Homogenization via annealing reduces these potential gradients, yielding a more uniform and protective oxide layer.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated Q235 steel, thermally annealed (homogenized) specimens will form a more uniform, adherent oxide film, exhibit delayed corrosion initiation, and show lower pit density and overall corrosion rates when exposed to the same harsh environments.
generation.baseline: Untreated Q235 steel in its as-received state forms a nonuniform iron oxide film that facilitates localized corrosion under chloride-rich and elevated temperature conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanistic behavior is predicted for Q235 steel exposed to corrosive environments dominated by chloride ions and moderate temperatures; the hypothesis may not extend to situations where additional protective coatings or alloying elements are present.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative impact of grain boundary reduction on the kinetics of passivation film formation and the exact role of minor inclusions or impurities in corrosion initiation remain partially uncertain. Variability in oxide film dynamics between room and elevated temperature conditions also contributes to the uncertainty.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Q235 steel specimens: one set in the as-received (untreated) condition and a second set subjected to a controlled thermal annealing process aimed at homogenizing the microstructure. Expose both sets to identical corrosive conditions (e.g., immersion in a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution) at room temperature and at an elevated temperature (approximately 60–100 °C) for a fixed period. Conduct periodic electrochemical tests (potentiodynamic polarization, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy) and perform surface analyses (SEM, EBSD) to assess oxide layer uniformity, pit density, and overall corrosion rate.
measurements: Corrosion rate (via weight loss and electrochemical impedance measurements)
Pit density and distribution (using scanning electron microscopy)
Uniformity and adherence of the oxide film (via surface characterization and cross-sectional SEM)
Grain size and grain-boundary density (using electron backscatter diffraction)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed (homogenized) Q235 specimens do not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in localized corrosion (i.e., similar corrosion rates, pit densities, and oxide film nonuniformity) compared to the untreated specimens, then the hypothesis that pre-exposure microstructural heterogeneity governs the onset of corrosion is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In this work, (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA were selected as the composition of coating because of its high strength and corrosion resistance in bulk state, while the corresponding properties of coating remain unknown. Therefore, (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating on the Q235 steel substrate was fabricated by using the plasma spray technique, and the microstructure evolution during preparation process, microhardness, and corrosion behavior in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution were investigated. Furthermore, the phase formation and the corrosion behavior of the coatings were specifically analyzed.

In this paper, the CoCrFeNiTix HEA coatings are prepared on Q235 steel substrate by laser cladding. The effect of Ti content on the microstructure and corrosion resistance in a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution was studied. Furthermore, the corrosion resistance mechanism was analyzed experimentally and by first-principles calculations.
